title: A11y-aware color blends and micro-elevation for layered interfaces
creator: Asha Patel
description: Rationalize and extend the design token set to introduce accessibility-aware blended accent ramps and a micro-elevation scale intended for layered interface patterns (flyouts, cards, toast stacking). This work covers color mixes for accessible contrast across light/dark themes, a 6-step micro-elevation token series with subtle shadow geometry, an updated responsive typography rhythm paired with token aliases, and small radius/spacing updates for density modes. Deliverables: token spec, Figma tokens, CSS/JSON token export, component usage guide, regression test suite.
acceptance_criteria: Color ramps include at least 5 blended accent steps with documented WCAG AA contrast against both surface and elevated backgrounds
Micro-elevation tokens (elev-0 .. elev-5) implemented in Figma and token export with pixel and rem shadow specs
Typography rhythm mapping updated and a fluid clamp spec provided for H1-H6, body and caption; tokens exported and verified in components
Spacing/radius token aliases for compact/comfortable density available and applied to Button, Table row, and Card components in the component playground
Automated visual regression baselines created for dark and light themes and runs added to CI; contrast tests pass for primary flows
decisions: Use blended HSL mixing to generate intermediate accent steps rather than hard-coded hex interpolation to preserve hue relationships across saturation changes
Micro-elevation will favor alpha-based colored shadows with tiny vertical offsets (0.5–6px) to remain visible on dark surfaces without creating halo artifacts
Typography will adopt clamp() fluid sizing for H2-H4 and tokenized step aliases to allow safe consumption by web and native teams
Do not increase the base corner radius; introduce radius aliases (radius-compact, radius-default, radius-pill) to support density rather than changing global base
open_questions: Should elev-3 use a slightly tinted shadow (surface tint) on light theme to improve separation for data-heavy tables? (ask Eng/PM)
Can infra expose a fast contrast check in the CI for visual diffs, or do we rely on storybook snapshots plus manual sampling?
What fallback behavior should Dedicated/Private deployments have for token-driven theming when customers override base tokens?
